extracted.intended_audience: candidates preparing for the French agrégation / ENS oral exams in algebra / advanced undergraduate students in algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Lesson outlines and oral-exam guidance for advanced algebra / linear algebra topics (polynomials, determinants, endomorphisms, matrix actions, exponentials), with jury remarks, questions, references and recommended examples. Intended to shape what a candidate should present in an oral lesson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic closure — definition and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Déf algébriquement clos, c’est équivalent à dire que tout polynôme est scindé; thm de d’Alembert-Gauss; R et les corps finis ne sont pas clos. Déf clôture algébrique, il en existe une. Exemples de C, de Q et de Fpn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lesson should define 'algébriquement clos', show equivalent formulations (every polynomial splits), mention existence of algebraic closures and classical examples/counterexamples (C is closed; R and finite fields are not), and connect to fundamental results (Gauss theorem).

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization and counting of roots — theorems and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclure théorèmes de Rolle (application aux polynômes scindés sur R), Gauss–Lucas, disques de Gershgörin (application à la matrice compagnon pour en déduire une condition de localisation des racines), théorème de Rouché (appliqué aux polynômes) et applications; Chevalley–Warning + EGZ mentionnés pour dénombrement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present several techniques for locating roots (real and complex), use companion matrix applications, give illustrative examples, and include counting results (Rouché applications, Chevalley–Warning) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetric polynomials — definitions, structure and algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Déf succincte des polynômes symétriques avec l’action de Sn et des polynômes symétriques élémentaires. Σp est p-homogène et de degré partiel 1 par rapport à chacune de ses variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not forget relations coefficients–racines; define weight and order, give structure theorem and decomposition algorithm, include Newton's identities and worked examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resultant and discriminant — definitions and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Déf du résultant sur un corps: R(P,Q) = 0 ssi ils ont un facteur commun; dans un corps algébriquement clos R(P,Q)=0 ssi P et Q ont une racine commune. Définition du discriminant via le résultant; Δ=0 ssi racine multiple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute discriminants for quadratics and cubics as examples; give Mérindol's 'formule magique des racines'; apply to Cayley–Hamilton, algebraic numbers (closure under + and ×) and elimination geometry (Bézout bound, intersection examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions on spaces of matrices — present invariants, algorithms, decompositions and orbit topology
rubrics_metrics.description: Présenter actions (translation, équivalence, conjugaison, congruence) avec invariants (rang, polynôme caractéristique/minimal), matrices compagnons, réduction de Frobenius, blocs de Jordan, théorème de Sylvester pour congruence, stabilisateurs, et dénombrement des orbites sur les corps finis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lesson should: exhibit invariants and algorithms (e.g. row-reduction, pivot de Gauss), give representatives of orbits (Jr, Jordan blocks), discuss orbit closures/topology over R/C, show counting on finite fields (cardinal of GL(n,K), orbit sizes), and indicate applications (LU decomposition, classification of conics, PFD, symplectic group). Include examples and references; jury notes ask for 'un certain recul'—highlight both algorithmic and theoretical viewpoints (decompositions, adhérences d’orbites).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension of a vector space — foundational theorems and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Bien connaître les théorèmes fondateurs de la théorie des espaces vectoriels de dimension finie en ayant une idée de leurs preuves; diverses caractérisations du rang et utilisation du degré d’une extension dans la théorie des corps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The jury expects careful proofs (not just statements); handle elementary but potentially tricky questions (e.g. subspace of a finite-dim space is finite-dim), present base incomplète theorem, Grassmann formula, and choose a coherent plan focused strictly on dimension (avoid unrelated topology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant — correct definition, geometric interpretation, and varied computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Il faut pouvoir, dans cette leçon, commencer par définir correctement le déterminant. Beaucoup de candidats entament la leçon en disant que le sous-espace des formes n-linéaires alternées sur un espace de dimension n est de dimension 1, ce qui est fort à propos. L’interprétation du déterminant comme volume est essentielle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define determinant via alternating n-linear forms, prove uniqueness (dim 1), show algebraic properties (multplicativity, invariance by base change), present geometric interpretation (volume, orientation), prove character polynomiality/continuity, present computational methods (Gaussian elimination, minors/cofactors, Sarrus, Vandermonde, Cauchy, circulant), but avoid giving only trivial examples (not only Vandermonde/circulant). Discuss determinant over Z (multimodular techniques possible), resultant and discriminant applications, and complexity remarks (Gauss pivot, complexity on Z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomials of an endomorphism (K[u]) and reduction — link polynomials ↔ endomorphism structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Déf du morphisme d’évaluation, de K[u] comme sous-algèbre de L(E), définition du polynôme minimal π_u; insister sur Krus ≃ K[X]/(π_u) via lemme chinois et lemme des noyaux; Ker(P(π_u)) stable par u.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize that properties of K[u] (and of π_u) are intrinsically linked to the endomorphism; use this to derive decomposition results (diagonalisation if π_u scindé à racines simples), trigonalisation criteria, Dunford decomposition, Frobenius reduction and Jordan form; provide constructive examples and show how to compute annihilating polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stable subspaces under endomorphisms and families — examples, reductions and simultaneous reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Définir sous-espace stable, bases adaptées; lemme des noyaux, interprétation comme diagonalisation par blocs; questions sur l’existence de supplémentaires stables (contre-exemples: bloc de Jordan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study detailed cases (diagonalisable, nilpotent of maximal index), use Frobenius decomposition, address commutation issues and simultaneous reduction (codiagonalisation/trigonalisation), and include applications to representation theory (Maschke) where appropriate; provide counterexamples to naive claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagonalizable endomorphisms — criteria, examples and topology/counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Donner des exemples naturels d’endomorphismes diagonalisables et des critères de diagonalisabilité; mentionner que sur certains corps la densité des matrices diagonalisables nécessite précisions; sur corps finis, critères et dénombrements spécifiques existent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat polynomial criteria (minimal polynomial has simple roots), criteria over finite fields, simultaneous diagonalization for commuting families, use spectral projectors for computations (e.g. exponentials), discuss density/topological subtleties over R/C and include counting/décompte on finite fields with examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix exponential — series convergence, computation methods and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Il faut pouvoir justifier clairement la convergence de la série exponentielle. Aborder questions de surjectivité/injectivité; la décomposition de Dunford multiplicative de exp(A) est utile; l’étude du logarithme (quand défini) trouve sa place; applications aux équations différentielles doivent être évoquées sans constituer l’essentiel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove normal convergence of the exponential series; show properties (exp(A+B)=exp(A)exp(B) if commute), compute via diagonalisation, Jordan blocks, or Dunford decomposition; study topological/differentiability properties of exp (continuity, diff'ble, local inversion theorem), relation with determinant and trace, address image of exp and classical examples/counterexamples, but avoid heavy Lie algebra topics unless well-mastered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of examples and choice of scope — jury expectations on lesson delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Rapport du jury: 'Cette leçon demande un certain recul... On peut aussi, si l’on veut aborder un aspect plus théorique, faire apparaître ...' ; for many lessons jury remarks stress that candidates must make choices, have coherent plan, and give non-trivial examples and proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must pick a coherent plan, prioritize foundational theorems with proofs, include illustrative and computational examples (not only trivial or single-pattern examples), be able to answer natural 'Questions' posed in the outline, and avoid drifting into topics outside the program unless clearly justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address specific 'Questions' and typical exam prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Each lesson contains explicit 'Questions' (e.g., show GL(n,Z) = {M in M_n(Z) | det(M) = ±1}; show θ is an algebraic integer iff Z[θ] has a finite generating family; examples about e^A being a polynomial in A, or whether certain matrices lie in the image of exp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A candidate should prepare to solve and present these concrete exercises/proofs during the oral: include them in the lesson or as follow-up exercises; they serve both as depth checks and as likely jury prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity, computational remarks and algorithmic aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions of algorithmic complexity (pivot de Gauss complexity O(n^3), Cramer complexity O(n!), multimodular methods for determinant over Z, practical methods for intersection via elimination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, indicate algorithmic costs or practical methods (Gaussian elimination, LU decomposition, multimodular approaches), and prefer effective algorithms in examples rather than purely theoretical computations.
